ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances fix the deviation. The trip was run at 14.8 km against a recommended route of 13.1 km, so under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is 1.70 km — above the 1.0 km tolerance that clause sets, which takes this case out of rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 and into a refund row. The GPS trace cannot rescue the driver here: POL-RD-22 states expressly that the trace is not used to re-measure the distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this trace carries only 45 fixes measuring 12.403 km, well under the recorded 14.8 km.

The trace's own map-matched road names confirm the reroute the trip record reports: the vehicle ran the Seletar Expressway to the Woodlands Avenue 12 exit, then Woodlands Avenue 12 and Sembawang Road from 08:23:43 through 08:32:13, before rejoining at Yishun Avenue 2 — matching the route_deviation_detected event at 08:23:17 and route_rejoined at 08:32:21. The driver's own account on file ('I took Sembawang Road') is consistent with this and with the rejoin event. The deviation was real, off the recommended route for roughly nine minutes.

The driver did not tell the rider anything about the deviation. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and the chat log holds only two messages, both sent before the trip started (08:10:23 driver, 08:10:38 rider) — nothing at or after the 08:23:17 deviation. The trip record's own messages_during_trip array is empty. The rider's acknowledgment that POL-RD-21 treats as agreement therefore does not exist on this record, and row (a) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply.

No trip call covers the gap either. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, so there is no recording from which a verbal notice could be established, and POL-RD-21 provides that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The only route by which the driver could have met the contact obligation was an in-app chat message, and none was sent during the trip.

The rider's recovery does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved, which is why this case fits a row of the matrix and no escalation is needed. If the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was not informed and row (b) of POL-RD-24 applies; if it was not traffic-justified, row (d) applies on a 1.70 km deviation. Both rows return the excess distance fare in full to the rider, so on either reading the rider must not carry the excess.

In any event the traffic justification is not made out on this record. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the advisory here overlaps the window but its own derived fields leave the intersection undetermined (intersects_route null, justifies_reroute null, and the artifact records the question 'on the recommended route' as unresolved). The advisory is also direction-specific — heavy traffic on the SLE 'towards TPE' — while the record nowhere states the direction the recommended route runs on the SLE, so the advisory's relevance to the route the trip was to take is unestablished. Under POL-RD-23 a driver's assertion of traffic that the data does not tie to the recommended route does not justify the reroute.

The sum the rider can properly recover under the matrix is the excess distance fare, computed as POL-RD-24 directs: 1.70 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.22 SGD, with no surge applied — the same figure the payments ledger's own derivation carries as excess_distance_fare_sgd. To that extent the rider's claim is supported and part of the trip's charge is returned. The 3.80 SGD stated in the claim exceeds what the matrix provides, because neither row (b) nor row (d) returns more than the excess distance fare.

Nothing on this record stands in the way of a final monetary ruling now. The contested amount is 3.80 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and both parties' fraud_flags are 0, so no confidence uplift to 0.95 is engaged; every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 imports no discount into the confidence; and POL-RD-25's extra 2 km ceiling is not applied and would not bite in any case on a 1.70 km deviation. The rider's claim should be determined on the merits, not held over.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23, and the driver's explanation does not rest on his word alone. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06004-01 is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC record for the Seletar Expressway (SLE), direction 'towards TPE', whose own span runs 'after Woodlands Ave 12 Exit' to the 'Yishun Avenue 2 exit' (valid 07:46:43-09:01:43). Those are the two points the trip record itself names for this deviation: the vehicle left the recommended route at 'SLE / Woodlands Avenue 12 exit' at 08:23:17 and rejoined it at 'Yishun Avenue 2 / Sembawang Road' at 08:32:21. On the record's own road and junction labels, the advisory covers the recommended SLE stretch the driver did not use. It also overlaps the trip window (08:11:43-08:33:43): overlaps_trip_window is true. HEAVY_TRAFFIC sits inside the policy's congestion vocabulary (route_deviation.thresholds.traffic_justification_types). The pre-pass left intersects_route and justifies_reroute for the Judge; on this record the answer is yes, so POL-RD-24's traffic-justified limb, and not the 'not traffic-justified' limb, is the one that applies to the driver's conduct.

The rider's 3.80 SGD claim is not what POL-RD-24 provides on any branch this record supports. The chat log EV-CHAT-06004 is complete and holds only the driver's 08:10:23 arrival notice and the rider's 08:10:38 'ok', both before the trip started; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is an empty list and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. No notice of the deviation was therefore given before or at the point of deviation as POL-RD-21 requires, so POL-RD-24(a) (informed and agreed, no refund) is not open. But that does not make the rider's claim good: the case falls in POL-RD-24(b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km), and even on the alternative POL-RD-24(d) (not traffic-justified) the measure is identical - the excess distance fare alone. Neither paying row returns any part of the trip fare beyond the excess distance fare, and neither returns the 3.80 SGD asked for; POL-GEN-03's PARTIAL_REFUND returns only the part of the trip's charge that is owed.

The recoverable sum is fixed by POL-RD-24's formula and not by the figure claimed: deviation_km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd. The deviation is 1.70 km, being the recorded actual distance 14.8 km minus the recorded optimal distance 13.1 km, which POL-RD-22 requires to be used rather than any re-measurement (13.0% over a 13.1 km route, and above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance). The per-km rate is 0.72 SGD (EV-FARE-06004). 1.70 x 0.72 = 1.22 SGD, rounded to the cent and with no surge on the excess (POL-RD-24's formula and notes; thresholds.excess_distance_fare.surge_applied is false). The ledger already carries that exact figure as excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.22. The most the rider can be returned on this record is therefore 1.22 SGD, and the 3.80 SGD he asks for is not the policy measure.

The trace confirms the deviation was brief and stayed on the recognised corridor, so the excess distance fare fully covers the rider's loss and there is no basis for anything larger. The driver's 45 fixes at 30 s intervals run SLE, then Woodlands Avenue 12 from 08:23:13, then Sembawang Road from 08:27:43, then back onto the recommended route at Yishun Avenue 2 at 08:32:43 and Yishun Central at 08:33:43, with no gap longer than 30 s and no fix worse than 8 m accuracy - about nine minutes off the recommended route in a 22-minute trip. POL-RD-22 permits the trace to be used for which route was taken and when, and requires the recorded distances to measure the deviation, which gives the 1.70 km and the 1.22 SGD excess already computed. Nothing in the record supports a refund of the trip fare or of the 3.80 SGD claimed.

ruling.explanation:
The rider's claim is partly right and partly overstated. The recommended route for TRP-06004 was 13.1 km and the trip was driven 14.8 km (EV-TRIP-06004), leaving the recommended Seletar Expressway (SLE) at the Woodlands Avenue 12 exit at 08:23:17 and rejoining at Yishun Avenue 2 at 08:32:21; the 45-fix trace (EV-GPS-06004) matches that route, and POL-RD-22 requires the platform's recorded distances to measure the deviation. The deviation is therefore 14.8 - 13.1 = 1.70 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance, so a refund row of POL-RD-24 applies and the tolerance rows (c) and (e) do not.

Notice of the deviation (POL-RD-21): the chat log EV-CHAT-06004 holds only the driver's 08:10:23 arrival message and the rider's 08:10:38 'ok', both before the 08:11:43 start; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. The driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, so row (a) ('informed and agreed') cannot apply.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23): the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06004-01 is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC record for the SLE 'towards TPE' covering the stretch from the Woodlands Avenue 12 exit to the Yishun Avenue 2 exit - the same two junctions the trip record uses for this deviation - and it overlaps the trip window (07:46:43-09:01:43 against 08:11:43-08:33:43, overlaps_trip_window true). On its road, direction and location it does intersect the recommended route, so the reroute is traffic-justified and row (b) applies. The argument that the advisory is not tied to the recommended route is not accepted on that location description.

The amount is the same either way: rows (b) and (d) both return the excess distance fare alone, and no row of POL-RD-24 returns any part of the trip fare. The excess distance fare is 1.70 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.22 SGD with no surge (thresholds.excess_distance_fare.surge_applied is false), which is also the figure the payments ledger carries (EV-FARE-06004, excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.22).

So of the 3.80 SGD the rider asked for, 1.22 SGD is returned and the balance of the fare stands; the driver is not owed any payment.

Confidence: every artifact carrying these facts (EV-TRIP-06004, EV-GPS-06004, EV-CHAT-06004, EV-FARE-06004, EV-ADVIS-06004-01) is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The contested amount is 3.80 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no 0.95 uplift; POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met and its 2 km ceiling is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false) and would not bite on a 1.70 km deviation. No referral clause applies to a route deviation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
